correctness.rationale: For N>=3 the Moore neighborhood has eight distinct sites. Every middle-column site of color i sees exactly a_(i+1)+b_(i+1)+c_(i+1) predator sites in three adjacent columns. The consequent 10-composition, 100-pair transfer counts ordered labeled states with weights 3!/(a0!a1!a2!), so F_N=tr(B^N) for every N>=3. From the exact generated 100x100 integer matrix, SymPy coefficient arithmetic verifies det(XI-B)=X^45(X-6)P18(X)Q18(X)^2. The graph has a 72-state primitive component and separate six-loop singleton; a certified Sturm bracket isolates the unique P root above 8, giving Perron dominance and exponential asymptotics. The exact checker also matches independent brute-force enumerations of every state on 3x3 and 3x4 rings. No extrapolation from finite experiments is used.

value.rationale: At threshold 4 the cyclic Moore model lies at the boundary between band propagation and observed large-domain fixation. Width-three periodic strips are the narrowest genuine eight-neighbor toroidal strips, making their entire stationary-state counting sequence and entropy a natural benchmark. The object-specific simplification to ten count types, exact degree-18 spectral factors and sharp exponential rate answer a nontrivial all-width invariant unavailable from finite basin simulations or a single-size census. No new generic transfer method is claimed; the value is the evaluated invariant and structural compression.
